input.title: Short complete notes
input.subject: Databases
input.content:
Atomicity makes a transaction an all-or-nothing operation.

Consistency preserves database rules before and after a transaction.

Isolation prevents concurrent transactions from observing intermediate changes.

Durability preserves committed changes after a restart.

A primary key uniquely identifies a row in a table.

A foreign key references a key in another table.

A primary key uniquely identifies a row in a table.

A foreign key references a key in another table.

An index can speed up reads but adds maintenance work to writes.

A rollback discards the changes of an uncommitted transaction.

A deadlock occurs when transactions wait on one another in a cycle.

Normalization reduces redundant storage of facts.

A backup is a separate copy used for recovery.

A transaction log records changes used during recovery.
